label: Surface warming in the permafrost zone
description: How much the ground surface warms from today to mid-century, where ESA shows permafrost (°C)
details: 2014–2023 → 2040–2069 · GIPL 2.0 ground surface · 5-model average · RCP 4.5 · outside the ESA permafrost zone counts as Low
method: Warming of the mean annual ground surface temperature: GIPL 2.0 surface temperature averaged over climate years 2040–2069 minus its average over 2014–2023 (the same "today" as the Permafrost Thaw Index), 5-model average, RCP 4.5. Only the change is used, never GIPL's temperature level, so no 0 °C threshold is involved. The GIPL files are labelled 20 years late (file year = climate year + 20). Only cells where ESA CCI Permafrost v5 shows permafrost in 2023 (permafrost fraction above 0) get a value; everywhere else there is no permafrost to thaw and the class is always Low. Inside the permafrost zone, GIPL's stuck cells and a 2 km border around them have no value. The surface is used rather than 1 m because thawing ground holds near 0 °C at depth while its ice melts, which hides the warming exactly where permafrost is closest to thawing.
sources: ESA CCI Permafrost v5 PFR 2023 (features_1km.nc pfr_2023)
author: Joshdpaul
retired: 2026-11-09 (Joshdpaul): wrong pattern. Surface warming is largest in the Arctic (Arctic amplification), which does not mean the permafrost there is thawing; the Interior and Seward Peninsula are known to have the highest thaw hazard. Its letter C was given to esa-plus-warming (never chosen as a team decision).
